title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Travel to learn, share more, and build inner authority
summary: Andreea Popa's August newsletter recaps Thunder's trips to Tallinn and Helsinki. She reports that Cris and colleagues went to observe how others build, and Cris concluded Thunder isn't missing much, only consistency and bravery in sharing its work. It also covers Cris's long-term dream of Thunder as a place where people start projects and get mentorship, plus Gabi's reflections on confidence and inner authority.

principles.text: Travel to see how others build, then bring back principles for the inside
principles.quote: He goes out looking for how things work on the outside and returns with a principle for the inside.

principles.text: Thunder already has what it needs; the gap is consistency and bravery in sharing its work
principles.quote: What we need is to be more consistent and a bit braver in getting outside our usual places in order to find out how far we can go and in trying to get more exposure for our work.

principles.text: Share knowledge, not just culture, and say yes before feeling ready
principles.quote: This is also good practice for talking about what we know, being seen, and saying yes even when we don’t feel completely ready.

principles.text: Keep putting yourself out there even when things go well, since good times aren't guaranteed
principles.quote: Meeting new people, sharing what we know, and building future relationships don’t always seem urgent.

principles.text: Cris's long-term dream: Thunder as a place to start projects and get mentorship
principles.quote: That one day Thunder might become a place where people not only come to work but also come to start new projects, meet other people, get mentorship, and find support as their ideas are still taking shape.

principles.text: Inner authority lets people disagree honestly without becoming enemies; relationships can survive truth
principles.quote: And perhaps that is one of the quiet ways in which relationships deepen - by discovering that the relationship can survive truth.
